{{Short description|Mathematical formalism describing knowledge of the world as patterns}}
{{About||"pattern theory" in pain science|Pain#Pattern_Theory|other meanings of "pattern"|Pattern (disambiguation)}}
{{more citations needed|date=January 2010}}
'''Pattern theory''', formulated by [[Ulf Grenander]], is a mathematical [[Formalism (mathematics)|formalism]] to describe knowledge of the world as [[pattern]]s. It differs from other approaches to [[artificial intelligence]] in that it does not begin by prescribing [[algorithm]]s and machinery to recognize and classify patterns; rather, it prescribes a vocabulary to articulate and recast the pattern concepts in precise language. Broad in its mathematical coverage, Pattern Theory spans [[algebra]] and [[statistics]], as well as local topological and global entropic properties.

In addition to the new algebraic vocabulary, its [[Statistics|statistical]] approach is novel in its aim to:
* Identify the [[Latent variable|hidden variables]] of a [[data set]] using real world data rather than artificial stimuli, which was previously commonplace.
* Formulate prior distributions for hidden variables and models for the observed variables that form the vertices of a [[Gibbs sampling|Gibbs]]-like graph.
* Study the randomness and variability of these graphs.
* Create the basic classes of [[stochastic]] models applied by listing the deformations of the patterns.
* Synthesize (sample) from the models, not just analyze signals with them.

The [[Brown University]] Pattern Theory Group was formed in 1972 by Ulf Grenander.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.dam.brown.edu/pattern/ug.html|title=Ulf Grenander's Home Page|date=January 22, 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090122102751/http://www.dam.brown.edu/pattern/ug.html|archive-date=2009-01-22}}</ref> Many mathematicians are currently working in this group, noteworthy among them being the [[Fields Medal]]ist [[David Mumford]].<ref>{{Cite arXiv|last=Mumford |first=David |date=2002-12-01 |title=Pattern theory: the mathematics of perception |eprint=math/0212400v1 }}</ref>  Mumford regards Grenander as his "guru"<ref>{{Cite web |title={{!}} Vision Introductory Comments |url=https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/mumford/vision/introvision.html |access-date=2025-12-13 |website=www.dam.brown.edu}}</ref> in Pattern Theory.
